chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, and others, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Zurara, who said:

I saw the nursemaid of Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) feeding him rice and striking it onto him, so what I saw grieved me. I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'I reckon your grief is due to what you saw from the nursemaid of Abu al-Hasan Musa.' I said to him, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said to me, 'Excellent is the food, rice; it expands the intestines and cuts off the hemorrhoids. And we envy the people of Iraq for their eating of rice and partially-ripened dates, for these two expand the intestines and cut off the hemorrhoids.'
ai.seo_question: What are the medical benefits of rice according to the Imams in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of the Imams, specifically Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) endorsement of rice (*al-aruzz*) for its digestive benefits, countering any initial surprise at its simple preparation. It underscores the Shia tradition of integrating daily dietary habits with spiritual and physical well-being, while also reflecting the geographical and agricultural context of Iraq, where rice and *busr* (semi-dried dates) were staple foods. The narration serves as a foundational text in Islamic dietary jurisprudence, validating the consumption of rice as a healthy, blessed sustenance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, and someone else, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, from Zurara who said,

‘I saw a nurse-maid of Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> being fed the rice, and she threw it upon him<sup>asws</sup>. So it grieved me, what I saw. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> reckon your grief is due to what you saw from a nursemaid of Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>’. I said, ‘Yes, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The best of the foods is the rice, it expands the intestine, and cuts off the hemorrhoids, and we envy the people of Al-Iraq with their eating of the rice, and partially-ripened dates, for these two expand the intestine and cut off the hemorrhoids’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma’il ibn Marrar and others from Yunus from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once saw the nurse of abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, feed him rice with morsels and threw it on him. It made me upset and I went to see abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who said to me, ‘I think what you have seen from the nurse of abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has made you upset.’ I replied, ‘Yes, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, food from rice expands the intestine and cuts down hemorrhoids. We deem people of Iraq as fortunate for their eating rice and fresh dates because they expand the intestine and cut down hemorrhoids.’”
